newsitem.title: USA: News Corp-TCI sports venture in Cablevision talks.
newsitem.headline: News Corp-TCI sports venture in Cablevision talks.

text.p: The sports cable TV joint venture of Liberty Media Corp. and News Corp.'s Fox Sports was in talks to buy a major stake in Cablevision Systems Corp.'s Rainbow cable unit for about $850 million, an industry source said Friday.

The talks were continuing, with an agreement possible by early next week, the source said. The venture would buy a stake of about 40 percent in Cablevision's Rainbow Programme Holding, the source said.
Spokesmen at Tele-Communications Inc., the Liberty parent, Liberty, Cablevision and Fox declined to comment. Liberty officials were not immediately available.
Rainbow includes the New York-area Madison Square Garden sports properties, which includes the famed sports arena, and MSG and SportsChannel cable networks.

The 50-percent joint venture, Fox-Liberty Networks, consists of nine regional owned-and-operated sports networks around the United States, including Fox Sports South, which has more than 6.1 million subscribers in Georgia, the Carolinas, Tennessee, Mississippi and Alabama. The venture also includes the FX cable channel.
News Corp. Chairman Rupert Murdoch has been seeking to build a competitor to ESPN, the U.S. sports cable channel, by cobbling together a group of owned-and-operated regional sports networks.
Rainbow is 75 percent owned by Cablevision, and 25 percent owned by General Electric Co.'s NBC unit.
ESPN and its ESPN2 networks are jointly owned by Walt Disney Co. and private Hearst Corp.
